Gihon (River of Eden)
GY-hon
proper noun
Hebrew Gichon, “bursting forth,” one of the four rivers that watered the garden of Eden, compassing the land of Cush.

Biblical Definition

The Gihon is the second of the four rivers of Eden, a witness to the goodness of the world as God first made it. From the garden a great water flowed and divided: “a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became into four heads” (Gen 2:10). The first was Pison, which “compasseth the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold” (Gen 2:11); “the name of the second river is Gihon: the same is it that compasseth the whole land of Ethiopia” (Gen 2:13); the third Hiddekel and the fourth Euphrates (Gen 2:14). These rivers preach the original bounty of creation, a world watered and gladdened by the hand of God before sin brought thorn and curse. The Gihon, whose name means “bursting forth,” poured its fullness over lands of gold and spice, a picture of unspoiled abundance. Eden’s rivers also point forward: as a river went out of Eden to water the garden, so from the throne of God flows the pure river of water of life, and the tree of life stands on its banks in the paradise restored (Rev 22:1-2). The Gihon of the first creation is a promise of the second. What Adam forfeited, the last Adam regains; the garden lost by sin is the garden-city gained by grace, watered for ever by the river of God.

Webster 1828 Definition

The second river of Eden, compassing the land of Cush (Gen 2:13); a witness to the original bounty of creation and a foretoken of the river of life in the paradise restored.

GIHON, the second of the four rivers of the garden of Eden.

Its name means “bursting forth.”

It compassed the whole land of Ethiopia, or Cush (Gen 2:13).

One of four heads into which Eden’s river parted (Gen 2:10).

A foretoken of the river of life in the paradise restored (Rev 22:1).

Key Scripture

Gen 2:13 — "And the name of the second river is Gihon: the same is it that compasseth the whole land of Ethiopia."

Gen 2:10 — "And a river went out of Eden to water the garden; and from thence it was parted, and became into four heads."

Gen 2:11 — "The name of the first is Pison: that is it which compasseth the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold;"

Gen 2:14 — "And the name of the third river is Hiddekel: that is it which goeth toward the east of Assyria. And the fourth river is Euphrates."

Modern Corruption

The second river of Eden; the entry recovers the historical goodness of the first creation and its promise fulfilled in the river of life.

expand to see more

Gihon belongs to the true history of the garden, and its chief modern corruption is the denial that Eden ever was. The four named rivers, two of them still known by name, anchor the account in geography, not myth. Scripture presents Eden as a real place with real waters, from which flowed the bounty of an unfallen world.

The corruption to name is the mythologizing of Genesis — the treatment of Eden and its rivers as legend or symbol rather than history. But the Holy Ghost names the Gihon, the Pison, the Hiddekel, and the Euphrates as He names any river of the earth, and the New Testament rests the whole doctrine of sin and salvation on a historical Adam in a historical garden (Rom 5:12-19). To dissolve Eden into fable is to loosen the ground of the gospel. The Gihon that watered the first paradise is the pledge of the river of life that waters the last, where the curse is gone and the tree of life bears its fruit for the healing of the nations.

Usage

"With Pison, Hiddekel, and Euphrates it watered the first garden."

"The Gihon preaches the goodness of creation and the promise of the river of life."
